papers.title: Learning the Influence of the Chemical Environment on Epoxy-Amine Cure Kinetics
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Accurate modelling of polymer-network formation requires describing reaction kinetics in a continuously evolving chemical environment. Epoxy-amine networks are a challenging model system: epoxy groups react successively with primary and secondary amines, while hydroxyl groups formed during cure promote autocatalysis. Semi-empirical models are easy to use, but always formulation-specific. Detailed mechanistic models provide a physically meaningful description by accounting for reactive and non-reactive complexes, but require numerous coupled reactions and parameters, limiting their extension to new formulations. Here, we develop a supervised learning framework for mechanistic model simplification. A physics-informed, fully connected residual neural Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) network maps the instantaneous chemical state to two effective reaction-rate coefficients, reducing a detailed 13-step epoxy-amine reaction scheme to the two major reactions describing epoxy consumption by primary and secondary amines. The reduced model retains the corresponding mass-balance equations and Arrhenius temperature dependence, while the neural network learns how the evolving chemical environment modifies reactivity. Temperature and the instantaneous concentrations of epoxy, primary, secondary and tertiary amines, and hydroxyl and ether functionalities are projected into a latent representation and processed through stacked residual blocks to predict the two rate constants. These coefficients are then used within the kinetic equations to predict complete cure trajectories. The network therefore does not directly predict conversion, but learns the unresolved influence of the chemical environment on physically interpretable kinetic parameters. Training data are generated with the detailed mechanistic model across a broad range of temperatures, stoichiometric ratios, ether concentrations and conversions. Effective rate coefficients derived from the simulated concentration trajectories are used to train the neural network. Data are split at the stoichiometric-ratio level: all complete cure trajectories associated with a given ratio are assigned exclusively to the training, validation or test set, preventing leakage between correlated conversion points and trajectories. Generalisation is evaluated on unseen stoichiometries and processing conditions using both the predicted rate coefficients and the resulting integrated cure trajectories. Network architecture and training parameters are selected through automated hyperparameter optimisation. In a subsequent experimental stage, the framework is fine-tuned and validated using heat-flow measurements from differential scanning calorimetry and microcalorimetry, complemented by near-infrared spectroscopy to track reactive-group concentrations in real time. The reduced model captures hydroxyl-induced autocatalysis, differences between primary- and secondary-amine reactivity, and variations in effective reaction rates with temperature, stoichiometry and ether concentration. It thus compresses a detailed reaction scheme into a computationally efficient model while preserving a physically interpretable kinetic mechanistic scheme. This hybrid approach provides a foundation for compact and transferable models of polymerization kinetics, combining data-driven representation of chemical-environment effects with mechanistic reaction equations.

papers.title: Combined Chemical and Physical Activation of Blast‐Furnace Slag Using Lime Kiln Dust: Mechanisms and Performance Enhancement
papers.abstract: Utilizing industrial by‐products as supplementary cementitious materials is an effective strategy for improving the sustainability of the construction industry. This study investigates a waste‐to‐waste approach in which lime kiln dust (LKD)—a fine particulate by‐product of lime calcination—is employed as a multifunctional activator to enhance the reactivity of ground granulated blast‐furnace slag (GGBS) in blended cement systems. GGBS–cement composites containing 0–7 wt.% LKD (replacing the corresponding proportion of the initial GGBS mass) were prepared by dry premixing, and their mechanical performance and hydration‐associated microstructural evolution were systematically examined. The 5 wt.% LKD mixture exhibited the highest 7 days activity index of 77.95%, whereas the 3 wt.% mixture exhibited the highest 28 days activity index of 99.62% and provided the best overall balance between early‐ and later‐age performance. The X‐ray diffraction, thermogravimetric and derivative thermogravimetric, Fourier‐transform infrared, and SEM observations are consistent with combined chemical and physical contributions from LKD. Chemically, CaO/Ca(OH) 2 in LKD may provide alkalinity that promotes the latent hydraulic reaction of slag, whereas CaCO 3 may participate in the formation of AFm‐type carboaluminate hydrates (Hc/Mc). Physically, fine LKD particles may act as microfillers and nucleation sites, consistent with the denser microstructure observed in the examined regions. Overall, the enhanced mechanical performance is consistent with concurrent chemical activation and LKD‐induced physical modification. These findings highlight LKD as a low‐cost and effective activator for GGBS and indicate potential environmental benefits associated with lower Portland‐cement demand and the coordinated utilization of the steel‐industry by‐products GGBS and LKD.

papers.title: Study on mechanical, corrosion and fractured surface of n-Mn modified Al5052 alloy: an ANOVA and ANN prediction of wear rate
papers.abstract: Aluminum (Al) 5052 alloys are extensively utilized in marine environments, pressure vessels, and automotive parts due to their better strength and low density. However, more investigation is required to comprehend how the nanoscale manganese (n-Mn) element affects their mechanical, tribological, corrosion, and machinability. The development of Al5052 alloy modified with n-Mn by increasing the weight percentage in 0.25% increments from 0 to 1% through stir casting is the main focus of this study. The nano-composite showed notable improvements in hardness (23.72%), tensile strength (11.01%), and corrosion resistance (57.69%). However, increasing the n-Mn content also led to a 77.35% increase in machining force and a 69.23% increase in surface roughness (Ra). Taguchi and ANOVA approaches were used to analyze the effects of n-Mn (wt. %), sample temperature (ºC), and sliding distance (m) on wear loss (g). The improved alloy's wear rate was largely influenced by its n-Mn concentration. Wear rate confirmation tests showed that maximum errors for the n-Mn modified Al5052 alloy were within permissible bounds. Additionally, the wear loss was successfully predicted using the proposed 3-4-1 Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. For the wear attributes taken into consideration, the predicted performance metrics produced mean squared errors (MSE) of 4.925*10-5 and R-squared values (R2) of 0.9361.

papers.title: Valorization of Mopa Mopa Resin as a Renewable Bio-Based Adhesion Promoter for Sustainable Wood Adhesives
papers.abstract: The search for renewable raw materials for developing wood adhesives has driven the study of natural resins with intrinsic adhesive properties. This work evaluated Mopa Mopa resin (Elaeagia pastoensis Mora) as an adhesion promoter in formulations for wood-to-wood bonding of pine. Initially, the individual behavior of the main components was assessed, and subsequently, nine systems were formulated by combining Mopa Mopa resin with polyvinyl acetate (PVAc), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA-OH), and starch. The selected formulations were compared with two commercial adhesives using shear and direct tensile strength tests, physical properties, FTIR, TGA, DSC, and fracture surface analysis. Mopa Mopa resin, evaluated individually, achieved a shear strength of 6.657 MPa, second only to that obtained with PVAc among the components studied. Following the initial screening stage, formulations F-3 and F-5 were selected and subsequently prepared as final adhesive systems containing 5.8% additives. Final formulation F-3 consisted of 54.2% PVAc, 20% Mopa Mopa resin, 20% PVA-OH, and 5.8% additives, whereas F-5 consisted of 29.5% PVAc, 37.5% Mopa Mopa resin, 27.2% cassava starch, and 5.8% additives. F-3 achieved a shear strength of 7.792 MPa, surpassing the commercial adhesive C1 (6.328 MPa), while F-5 achieved the highest average direct tensile strength (1.371 MPa). Physicochemical characterization confirmed the presence of functional groups associated with the formulation components, while fracture analysis of F-3 revealed cohesive, mixed, and substrate failures. Taken together, the results demonstrate the potential of Mopa Mopa resin as a functional component and adhesion promoter in wood formulations, allowing its combination with synthetic polymers and renewable raw materials to obtain bonds with competitive mechanical performance.

papers.title: Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysts with Trinuclear, Mixed‐Valence Iron Motifs on Electronically Aligned Carbon Dots
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a bottleneck for water electrolysis, remains limited by the adsorbate scaling relations and sluggish interfacial electron transfer (IET). We address these challenges by anchoring mixed‐valence Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ motifs on aspartic‐acid–derived carbon dots (AspCDs). Spectroscopic analyses support trinuclear Fe 3 sites, which offer redox flexibility and proximal active centers. The Fe 3 site binds the substrate (OH − ) and is electronically coupled to the AspCD scaffold. Together with the work function‐aligned scaffold for electron abstraction from OH − , these features establish effective inner‐sphere IET from OH − , through the active Fe 3 center and the AspCDs host to the electrode. Simultaneously, the mixed valency buffers the charge build‐up during the successive proton‐coupled electron transfers. The catalyst drives fast and selective O 2 generation and minimizes H 2 O 2 formation, while sustaining at least ∼70 h of continuous operation with a gradual ∼90 mV total potential increase. Thus, the Fe 3 /AspCDs catalyst requires only 110 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm −2 , shows particularly effective kinetics with a low Tafel slope of 41 mV dec −1 , and has a turnover frequency of 2.1 s −1 . The design integrates crucial physicochemical properties for highly efficient OER, and the principle can be generalized to other systems toward further advances in the field.

papers.title: Epoxy Composites With Improved Thermal Conductivity and Low Viscosity for Electronic Packaging via Nanodiamond‐Decorated Boron Nitride Nanosheets
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electronic packaging underfill materials require high thermal conductivity (TC) and low viscosity, but combining these in epoxy (EP) remains a critical bottleneck. Prefabricated skeleton networks or high filler content enhance EP's TC yet severely compromise viscosity. Therefore, improving TC at a relatively low filler content without significantly sacrificing viscosity is highly desirable. Here, a dense, uniform layer of nanodiamonds (ND) is decorated on the boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS) surface to fabricate BNNS@ND, which is then incorporated into EP to develop a BNNS@ND/EP composite. The anchored ND is proposed to suppress BNNS stacking, thereby favoring uniform dispersion of BNNS@ND and the formation of continuous heat‐conducting pathways at relatively low filler content in EP. The ND coating is also considered to improve interfacial compatibility between BNNS and EP, as well as to alleviate the viscosity increase of EP composite associated with BNNS stacking. Consequently, compared to pure EP, incorporating merely 30 phr BNNS@ND increases the TC by 522.2% to 1.12 W/(m·K) and raises the glass transition temperature ( T g ) by 25.1% to 133.8°C of BNNS@ND/EP, while the composite retains a low viscosity of 16.7 Pa·s. This work offers a feasible approach for electronic‐packaging polymer composites with exceptional TC, T g , and viscosity.

papers.title: Influence of hybrid lignocellulosic fillers on processing, microstructure, mechanical and thermal behavior of kenaf/epoxy composites
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part E Journal of Process Mechanical Engineering
papers.abstract: The large-scale generation of agricultural residues such as pine needle (PN) and citrus peel waste poses environmental and disposal challenges. This study investigates the valorization of these lignocellulosic wastes as hybrid bio-fillers in kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy composites, establishing a sustainable waste-to-material conversion pathway. PN and citrus limetta peel (CLP) particulates were incorporated individually and in hybrid configurations to evaluate their influence on mechanical and thermal performance, flammability behavior, and moisture-related dimensional stability. Mechanical characterization showed that both single and hybrid PN/CLP filler configurations improved the mechanical performance relative to the unfilled kenaf/epoxy reference, with the magnitude of improvement depending on filler type and the PN:CLP ratio. Among the investigated formulations, the KE-CLP10 composite exhibited an increase of approximately 47% in tensile strength, 26% in tensile modulus, and 80% in impact strength relative to the reference composite. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated enhanced thermal stability, with the hybrid composites exhibiting residual char contents of approximately 13% to 18%. Water absorption studies showed composition-dependent moisture uptake, with selected hybrid formulations exhibiting lower water absorption and improved dimensional stability relative to the neat kenaf/epoxy reference. The findings demonstrate that underutilized PN and citrus peel residues can be effectively converted into value-added reinforcing materials, improving composite durability while contributing to resource circularity and sustainable materials engineering.

papers.title: Adaptive Radiotherapy: Principles, Technologies, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions — A Comprehensive Review
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Adaptive radiotherapy (ART) represents a paradigm shift in radiation oncology, enabling real-time or iterative modification of treatment plans in response to anatomical, physiological, and biological changes occurring throughout the course of treatment.Unlike conventional radiotherapy, which relies on a single pre-treatment plan, ART dynamically adjusts beam delivery to account for inter-and intrafraction variations in tumor volume, shape, and position, as well as changes in surrounding normal tissues and organs at risk (OARs) .Methods: A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 to December 2024, using the MeSH terms 'adaptive radiotherapy,''online adaptation,''offline adaptation,''image-guided radiotherapy,''MR-linac,' and 'cone-beam CT.' A total of 148 peerreviewed articles, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and clinical guidelines were screened; 102 met the inclusion criteria and are cited herein.Results: Evidence from randomized and observational studies demonstrates that ART reduces radiation dose to OARs by 10-35% compared with conventional radiotherapy while maintaining equivalent or superior tumor control rates.Emerging magnetic resonance-guided linac (MR-linac) technologies and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven automated re-planning systems have substantially reduced online adaptation workflow times to under 30 minutes, enabling clinical scalability.Conclusion: ART is rapidly becoming the standard of care for anatomically complex and motion-sensitive malignancies including head and neck, prostate, cervical, and lung cancers.Continued innovation in imaging, automation, and biological adaptation promises to further enhance therapeutic ratios and patient outcomes.

papers.title: Bamboo particleboards bonded with lignin-modified vinyl acetate-ethylene adhesive: physical, mechanical, and thermal properties
papers.journal: European Journal of Wood and Wood Products
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of sustainable adhesive systems based on renewable resources is essential for advancing environmentally friendly lignocellulosic materials. However, limited information is available on the direct modification of vinyl acetate-ethylene (VAE) adhesives with Kraft lignin for bamboo particleboards, particularly regarding the relationship between adhesive thermal behavior, interfacial morphology, and panel performance. This study evaluated the effect of incorporating Kraft lignin (0, 5, 10, 15, and 20%) into VAE adhesive on the physical, mechanical, morphological, and thermal properties of bamboo particleboards. TGA/DTG and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used to investigate adhesive thermal behavior and particle–adhesive interfacial morphology, respectively. Lignin incorporation was associated with improved dimensional stability and mechanical performance. Water absorption decreased from 17.04% to 6.62% after 2 h and from 80.31% to 36.29% after 24 h. At 15% lignin, the modulus of rupture, modulus of elasticity, and internal bond increased from 38.02 to 60.45 MPa, 2219 to 5449 MPa, and 0.31 to 0.68 MPa, respectively. TGA/DTG showed that lignin did not substantially alter the overall degradation profile of VAE but increased carbonaceous residue at high temperatures. SEM revealed improved interfacial cohesion up to 15% lignin, with reduced fiber pull-out, fewer voids, and a more continuous adhesive matrix, whereas 20% lignin promoted agglomeration and microvacuole formation. Thermal conductivity remained stable at 0.13–0.15 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. Among the formulations evaluated, 10 and 15% Kraft lignin showed the most favorable combination of dimensional stability and mechanical performance, demonstrating the potential of lignin as a renewable modifier for VAE-based bamboo particleboards.

papers.title: Upper Flammability Limits of Methane/Air Mixtures at Elevated Temperature and Pressure
papers.abstract: Abstract Methane/air mixtures in preheated and pressurized process equipment may exhibit a broadened flammability envelope, which is critical for explosion-hazard assessment and safety-envelope definition. Reliable upper flammability limit (UFL) data under elevated-temperature and elevated-pressure conditions are therefore needed for methane-related industrial systems. In this work, the UFLs of methane/air mixtures were measured in a 20 L closed spherical vessel at initial temperatures of 25–100 °C and pressures of 0.1–1.0 MPa in accordance with EN 17624:2022 and GB/T 42368–2023. Within the investigated range, the UFL increases approximately linearly with temperature and logarithmically with pressure. Under simultaneous temperature and pressure elevation, the increase in UFL is greater than that estimated from the simple superposition of their individual effects, indicating a non-negligible interaction between the two parameters. Based on the full experimental matrix, an empirical correlation incorporating a temperature–pressure interaction term is proposed to represent the UFL surface and shows good agreement with the experimental data. Chemical-kinetic simulations using USC Mech II were performed to assist interpretation of the experimental trends. The normalized sensitivity analysis identifies temperature-promoted branching pathways and pressure-enhanced radical stabilization/recombination pathways as the principal competing kinetic tendencies near the UFL. The present work provides a protocol-compliant methane/air UFL data set and a practical correlation for preheated and pressurized methane systems.

papers.title: An Intelligent Hybrid Model for Predicting Building Thermal Load from Geometric and Envelope Attributes
papers.abstract: Prediction of building thermal loads is vital for improving energy-efficient building design, sustainable infrastructure planning, and intelligent energy management in modern civil engineering applications. Existing thermal load prediction models often struggle to attain nonlinear dependencies and feature interactions in structured building datasets. Several existing studies also focus primarily on component-level thermal analysis or restricted climatic conditions, reducing broader prediction generalization and interpretability. To overcome these limitations, this model introduces a hybrid TabNet-ResMLP approach combined with interaction-based analysis to provide interpretable insights into the influence of geometric and envelope parameters on building thermal load. TabNet was employed for attentive feature selection and contextual feature weighting, while ResMLP performed residual nonlinear regression for modelling complex thermal behavior. The proposed model was validated using the Energy Efficiency dataset. Experimental evaluation achieved Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) values of 1.65 and 1.95, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values of 1.12 and 1.38, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) values of 6.0% and 7.1%, and Coefficient of Determination (R²) values of 0.98 and 0.97 for Heating Load (HL) and Cooling Load (CL), respectively. Feature importance, sensitivity, and interaction analyses further identified relative compactness, Surface Area (SA) and Overall Height (OH) as dominant parameters influencing thermal demand variation. The findings establish the efficacy of the proposed framework for early-stage building energy assessment, sustainable architectural design, and energy-efficient building operation.
papers.summary: Prediction of building thermal loads is vital for improving energy-efficient building design, sustainable infrastructure planning, and intelligent energy management in modern civil engineering applications. The proposed model was validated using the Energy Efficiency dataset. The findings establish the efficacy of the proposed framework for early-stage building energy assessment, sustainable architectural design, and energy-efficient building operation.

papers.title: Remote Sensing-based Integration of Land Use/Land Cover, Vegetation Cover, and Land Surface Temperature with Hydrological Implications in Tikrit City, Iraq
papers.abstract: This study examines the integrated relationship among Land Use/Land Cover (LULC), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and Land Surface Temperature (LST), with hydrological implications, in Tikrit City, Iraq, using Landsat data acquired in 2017 and 2025. LULC, NDVI, and LST layers were prepared using the same spatial boundary, and 4124 paired sample points were extracted from identical locations to support temporal and statistical comparison. The LULC results showed a clear reduction in Soil from 70.52% in 2017 to 49.88% in 2025, whereas Vegetation increased from 25.49% to 44.12%. Built Area also increased from 3.08% to 4.90%, indicating moderate urban expansion. The dominant land-cover transition was from Soil to Vegetation, covering 66,014.66 ha. Mean NDVI increased significantly from 0.061 to 0.075, while mean LST remained statistically stable, changing only from 41.992°C to 42.031°C. However, non-parametric tests indicated that the spatial distribution of LST changed significantly. The NDVI–LST relationship was positive in both years, with Pearson correlation increasing from 0.670 in 2017 to 0.709 in 2025. Regression analysis showed that NDVI explained 44.9% and 50.2% of LST variation in 2017 and 2025, respectively. Class-based analysis indicated that the dominant heat-contributing class shifted from Soil in 2017 to Built Area in 2025. These findings show that surface thermal behavior in Tikrit City cannot be explained by vegetation cover alone, but depends on land-cover composition, mixed pixels, agricultural activity, soil exposure, surface moisture, and seasonal conditions. From a hydrological perspective, the reduction of exposed soil, expansion of vegetation, and growth of built-up areas have implications for infiltration opportunity, runoff potential, evapotranspiration tendency, and surface moisture retention.

papers.title: Engineering a multifunctional bioactive coordination polymer nanoplatform for inflammation-responsive bone regeneration
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bone diseases are closely associated with impaired osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and excessive inflammatory signaling. Sinomenine (SIN) exhibits anti-inflammatory activity; however, its therapeutic application is limited by poor bioavailability. In this work, a multifunctional nanoplatform (CS-1@CP1@SIN) was constructed for SIN delivery and electrochemical sensing applications. The nanocomposite exhibited a mesoporous structure, structural stability, and improved electrochemical response characteristics. In a TNF-α-induced inflammatory MSC model, CS-1@CP1@SIN improved cell viability, reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6), and enhanced the expression of osteogenic markers (Runx2, ALP, and OCN). In addition, the CS-1@CP1@SIN-modified electrode exhibited enhanced electrocatalytic activity toward tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ), enabling sensitive and reliable electrochemical detection. These results demonstrate that the proposed nanoplatform integrates anti-inflammatory therapy and electrochemical sensing functions, providing a multifunctional strategy for inflammatory bone disease treatment and food antioxidant monitoring.

papers.title: Efficient one-pot synthesis of molybdenum dialkyl dithiocarbamate and investigation on evolution mechanism of tribofilms in ester-based lubricants
papers.abstract: Abstract Base oil polarity critically governs additive solubility, interfacial adsorption, and tribochemical reactions, which collectively determine friction, wear, and component service life. In this study, molybdenum dialkyldithiocarbamate (MoDTC) was synthesized via a facile one-pot route. Its dispersion stability and tribological properties were compared in two base oils with distinct polarities: polar diisooctyl sebacate (DIOS) and nonpolar polyalphaolefin (PAO6). The tribological behavior of the MoDTC/DIOS blend was further evaluated under variable applied loads and temperatures. The results reveal that MoDTC delivers superior friction-reducing and anti-wear performance in nonpolar PAO6, attributed to stable adsorption on friction surfaces and tribochemical decomposition into protective tribofilms. In contrast, polar DIOS enables the MoDTC/DIOS blend to reach a steady friction coefficient (COF) much faster, with a drastically shortened running-in stage. Cross-sectional characterizations demonstrate that the polar DIOS environment accelerates MoDTC decomposition and rapid formation of an amorphous Mo- and S-containing tribofilm, accounting for the sharp COF decline. Nevertheless, this amorphous tribofilm exhibits low load-bearing capacity and cannot effectively suppress interfacial wear, resulting in a larger wear scar diameter (WSD) than the MoDTC/PAO6 blend. At 25 °C, MoDTC achieves optimal lubrication, reducing the COF and WSD of neat DIOS by 50.0% and 23.3%, respectively. At 75 °C, COF reduction reaches 61.5%; at 125 °C, despite severe fluctuations in the friction curve, the WSD remains smaller than that of neat DIOS, indicating sustained anti‑wear capability. Combined with multiple modern characterizations, the underlying lubrication mechanisms is clarified: at low‑to‑medium temperatures, MoDTC preferentially generates a dense tribofilm dominated by layered MoS2; at elevated temperatures, the tribofilm transforms into a composite of MoO3 and MoSxOy. Despite increasing the COF, this composite tribofilms retain excellent load‑bearing and anti‑adhesion properties to mitigate severe wear. This study provides guidance for optimizing MoDTC synthesis, polarity matching, and tribofilm regulation, facilitating its wide application in lubrication systems.

This study provides guidance for optimizing MoDTC synthesis, polarity matching, and tribofilm regulation, facilitating its wide application in lubrication systems.

papers.title: Advancements in Fonio (Digitaria exilis): Emerging Insights into Horticultural Development, Bioactive Composition, Functional Properties, and Drug Delivery Potential
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Fonio (Digitaria exilis) is an ancient orphan cereal of West Africa which has been recently highlighted in the scientific literature around the world because of its unique nutritional characteristics, its resistance to the adverse abiotic conditions and also its potential therapeutic uses.The present review summarizes and consolidates the knowledge regarding the horticultural and genomic development, bioactive composition, functional properties, and pharmaceutical delivery systems from peer-reviewed publications published between 2020 and 2025.The genomic progress contains the release of a high quality tetraploid reference genome, the understanding of independent domestication pathways for white and black fonio, and agro-morphological characterization of germplasm diversity.Bioactive Profiling shows the presence of sulfur containing amino acids (methionine and cysteine) at about 150 and 350 mg/kg respectively, flavones such as apigenin and luteolin at about 150 antidiabetic (animal studies), anti-inflammatory (flavonoids), and glutenfree.In the pharmaceutical sector, the cross-linked fonio starch nanoparticles (180-320 nm) have been shown to have high papers.title: Investigating Electro-Thermal Distribution in High-Capacity Large-Format Blade Batteries for Energy Storage
papers.abstract: Batteries are regarded as a uniform heat source in traditional thermal management system design. Inconsistencies in electrochemical reactions across time and space are often ignored, which leads to an unreasonable battery thermal management system. This paper establishes a 2D electro-thermal fully coupled model based on the Kim model and NTGK model for a high-capacity blade battery. Based on the experimental results, the accuracy of the model was verified by examining terminal voltage, average battery temperature, and temperature distribution. The distribution characteristics of physical fields within the battery were analyzed using the electro-thermal model. The results indicated that the distribution of electrochemical reaction rates inside the battery shows a clear boundary between the near-tab area and the middle positions. In the initial stage of discharge, the electrochemical reaction rates were higher around the tabs. However, the electrochemical reaction rates were higher around the middle positions at the end stage of discharge. Thus, we proposed two schemes, a three-zone model and a five-zone model for 3D thermal analysis, according to the distribution characteristics of the physical fields. We found that the difference in the prediction accuracy of temperature distribution between the two schemes was small. Therefore, we recommended the three-zone scheme for 3D thermal analysis, considering the complexity of the operation. These conclusions could provide a reference for a refined thermal management system design of large-sized blade batteries.

papers.title: Prediction of temperature field indicators of concrete bridges based on the Informer model
papers.abstract: Accurate assessment of bridge temperature distributions is essential for evaluating structural safety. To predict bridge temperature field indicators, this study proposes an Informer-based forecasting method. Structural temperature field data are generated through finite element thermal analysis, and the two-dimensional temperature field at a representative cross section is decomposed into four physically meaningful indicators. These indicators are combined with time and meteorological features to construct a sample database for model development and evaluation. The results show that, compared with the typical time-series forecasting models LSTM and ARIMA, the Informer model achieves higher accuracy in single-step prediction. As the forecast horizon increases, the prediction accuracy of Informer decreases to some extent but remains relatively high at the 24-h forecast horizon. Based on these evaluation results, a rolling prediction method with a 24-h cycle is developed, enabling continuous forecasting of bridge temperature field indicators.

Based on these evaluation results, a rolling prediction method with a 24-h cycle is developed, enabling continuous forecasting of bridge temperature field indicators.

papers.title: Cu 2 ⁺-responsive hyaluronic acid nanoplatform for targeted curcumin delivery and suppression of osteolysis- and metastasis-related phenotypes in lung adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Bone metastasis is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in lung adenocarcinoma and is closely associated with epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) and tumor-derived osteolytic factors. Although curcumin exhibits promising anti-tumor and anti-metastatic activities, its poor solubility and low bioavailability limit its therapeutic application. In this study, a Cu 2 ⁺-responsive hyaluronic acid nanoplatform modified with compound 1 (1-HA) was developed for targeted curcumin delivery (1-HA@Cur) and Cu 2 ⁺-responsive fluorescence sensing. The physicochemical properties, Cu 2 ⁺ sensing performance, and biological effects of 1-HA@Cur were systematically evaluated under in vitro conditions using A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells. Compared with free curcumin, 1-HA@Cur exhibited enhanced antiproliferative activity and induced a significant dose-dependent reduction in cell viability. Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) analysis demonstrated that nanoparticle treatment significantly decreased the secretion of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP), a key mediator involved in osteolytic signaling. Furthermore, qRT-PCR analysis revealed that 1-HA@Cur modulated EMT-associated molecular changes, characterized by reduced Vimentin expression and increased E-cadherin expression. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 1-HA@Cur effectively suppresses lung adenocarcinoma cell growth and attenuates osteolytic- and metastasis-related phenotypes in vitro . This multifunctional nanoplatform integrates targeted curcumin delivery with Cu 2 ⁺-responsive fluorescence sensing, providing a potential strategy for lung adenocarcinoma therapy and copper-ion-associated microenvironment analysis, while further validation in more complex biological models is required.

The physicochemical properties, Cu 2 ⁺ sensing performance, and biological effects of 1-HA@Cur were systematically evaluated under in vitro conditions using A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 1-HA@Cur effectively suppresses lung adenocarcinoma cell growth and attenuates osteolytic- and metastasis-related phenotypes in vitro .

papers.title: Nose-to-Brain Nanoformulations for Enhanced Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease: Design, Optimization, and Evaluation of Mucoadhesive Chitosan-Coated Nanostructured Lipid Carriers of Donepezil Hydrochloride
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive, irreversible neurodegenerative disorder representing the most prevalent cause of dementia worldwide.Conventional oral pharmacotherapy with donepezil hydrochloride (DPZ) faces significant impediments including extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism, limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, and systemic adverse effects that collectively restrict therapeutic efficacy.The present investigation aimed to design, optimize, and characterise mucoadhesive chitosan-coated nanostructured lipid carriers (CS-NLCs) loaded with donepezil hydrochloride for intranasal nose-to-brain delivery, employing a Quality by Design (QbD) framework through Box-Behnken Design (BBD) to circumvent BBB limitations and enhance olfactory neuronal transport.CS-NLCs were fabricated using a hot homogenisation-ultrasonication method.A three-factor, three-level Box-Behnken experimental design was applied, with lipid concentration, surfactant concentration, and chitosan concentration as independent variables, and particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), zeta potential, entrapment efficiency (EE%), and cumulative drug release as responses.Comprehensive physicochemical characterisation was performed, including dynamic light scattering, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).In vitro drug release was studied using the dialysis bag method in simulated nasal fluid (SNF).Ex vivo permeation studies were conducted using freshly excised goat nasal mucosa.Cytotoxicity was evaluated using MTT assay on SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma and RPMI 2650 nasal epithelial cells.Molecular docking studies were performed against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and beta-secretase-1 (BACE-1) using AutoDock Vina.The optimised CS-NLC formulation (F9) exhibited a particle size of 178.4 ± 3.2 nm, PDI of 0.182 ± 0.012, zeta potential of +28.6 ± 1.4 mV, entrapment efficiency of 87.3 ± 1.6%, and cumulative drug release of 82.4 ± 2.1% over 24 h following Korsmeyer-Peppas kinetics (n = 0.68, indicating anomalous diffusion).Ex vivo permeation studies demonstrated a flux of 42.8 ± 2.3 μg/cm²/h and a permeability coefficient of 2.14 × 10⁻³ cm/h, approximately 3.7-fold higher than plain DPZ solution.Mucoadhesive strength was 14.8 ± 1.2 mN, and mucin binding efficiency reached 76.8 ± 2.4%.Cell viability exceeded 85% at therapeutic concentrations on both cell lines.Molecular docking revealed binding affinities of -8.6 kcal/mol (AChE) and -7.9 kcal/mol (BACE-1).The mucoadhesive CS-NLC platform demonstrated superior physicochemical characteristics, sustained release, enhanced nasal permeation, and satisfactory safety profiles, suggesting its significant potential as an effective nose-to-brain drug delivery system for Alzheimer's therapy.This study was conducted entirely through in vitro and ex vivo approaches, ethically minimizing animal usage.

papers.title: Effect of Sulfonate-, Phosphonate-, and Lipoate-Functional Modifiers on the Mechanical and Thermal Properties of Polymethyl Methacrylate Denture Base Resin
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the mechanical and thermal properties of heat-polymerized polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) denture base resin modified with different concentrations of sodium 4-styrenesulfonate (SO), 5,5-bis(diisopropoxyphosphoryl)pentyl methacrylate (PO), and 5,5-bis(diisopropoxyphosphoryl)pentyl lipoate (LIP). Materials and Methods: Heat-polymerized PMMA specimens were divided into a control group and experimental groups modified with 2%, 3%, or 5% SO, PO, or LIP (n = 8 per group). Maximum deflection, flexural strength, and Young’s modulus were determined using a three-point bending test. Surface hardness was evaluated using the Vickers hardness test, thermal behavior was assessed by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and fracture surfaces were examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA (modifier type × concentration) with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons, and comparisons including the control group were performed using Welch’s or one-way ANOVA followed by Tamhane’s T2 or Bonferroni post hoc tests, depending on the homogeneity of variances (α = 0.05). Results: Modifier type significantly affected maximum deflection, flexural strength, Young’s modulus, and Vickers hardness of specimens. The LIP-containing groups showed the highest mean deflection values but significantly lower flexural strength, Young’s modulus, and hardness than the control group. In contrast, the SO-containing groups generally maintained mechanical properties closer to those of unmodified PMMA. TGA showed that all modifiers altered the thermal degradation profile of PMMA, with PO increasing the main degradation temperature by approximately 40 °C. Conclusions: The investigated modifiers produced distinct, modifier-dependent changes in the mechanical and thermal behavior of heat-polymerized PMMA. Although LIP increased deformation capacity, this occurred at the expense of flexural strength and stiffness. SO and PO modifications showed comparatively smaller changes in mechanical properties at selected concentrations. Further studies including direct fracture-toughness, fatigue, and clinically relevant aging assessments are required to determine whether these modifications provide functional advantages for denture base applications.

papers.title: Bulky‐Group‐Functionalized Bidentate Pt(II) Complexes With Aggregation‐Induced Emission for Blue Phosphorescent Organic Light‐Emitting Diodes
papers.abstract: Pt(II) metal complexes with aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) properties are creating new opportunities in the fields of optoelectronics and their applications. We synthesized a series of AIE‐active sky blue and bluish green Pt(II) complexes with varying structures, such as (Pt1–Pt4). Their photophysical, electrochemical, thermal, and electroluminescence properties were systematically investigated. The suppression of low‐energy excimer emission in (Pt1–Pt4) was confirmed by PL studies of neat films. This is due to the introduction of bulky trityl and diphenyl phosphine oxide Ph 2 (P═O) in the main ligand and di‐mesityl groups on the ancillary ligand. All the complexes exhibited better photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQYs) in the film state. Consequently, the phosphorescent organic light‐emitting (PHOLED) device with Pt2 as a dopant achieved a maximum current efficiency (CE) of 20 cd/A and a power efficiency (PE) of 14.4 lm/W at a 10 wt% doping ratio, outperforming Pt1 (CE:7.5 cd/A, PE:5.3 lm/W at 15 wt%). Notably, the vacuum deposition PHOLEDs demonstrated significantly superior performance compared to their solution‐processed counterparts. This work provides a foundation for future research into AIE/AIEE‐active emitters for advanced display applications.
papers.summary: Pt(II) metal complexes with aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) properties are creating new opportunities in the fields of optoelectronics and their applications. papers.title: Supramolecular structuring of nanoparticle ligand shells revealed by liquid-phase AFM
papers.abstract: Abstract Polymer grafts are a ubiquitous component of nanocrystal (NC) ligand shells and impart critical functionalities, including biocompatibility and colloidal stability. Although many techniques have been used for elucidating the supramolecular structure of polymer chains once grafted to the NC surface, few of these are able to provide a complete picture of the ligand shell under experimentally relevant conditions ( e.g ., low polymer densities, various solvent environments). Here, we use high-resolution atomic force microscopy imaging along with coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to directly image polymers grafted onto single Ag NCs in both air and water to better understand the ligand-solvent interactions that dictate ligand shell structuring. For hydrophobic grafts under poor solvent conditions, the grafts self-associate to form a patchy shell, as previously reported. However, for hydrophilic grafts under good solvent conditions, this patchy morphology persists and is observed even for polyethylene glycol-functionalized NCs (i.e. PEGylated) in water. Polymer structuring is also observed amongst assembled NCs, with the formation of polymer bridges forming across patches. These unexpected results suggest that surface patchiness may be more widespread in colloidal NC systems than previously assumed, and this surface heterogeneity could play an important role in governing collective NC phenomena such as self-assembly.

papers.title: Applications of Phase Change Materials (PCMs) in Occupational Clothing Textiles
papers.journal: International Journal on Humanities and Social Sciences
papers.abstract: Phase change materials (PCMs) are increasingly proposed for occupational clothing, either to delay heat transfer to the skin during thermal hazard exposure or to relieve heat strain during work in hot environments. This critical review examines PCMs incorporated through three distinct routes: fiber, yarn, or fabric incorporation; coatings and laminated structures; and removable packs or modules and follows each from material properties through garment construction and heat and moisture transfer to wearer outcomes and maintenance. The evidence comes mainly from firefighting and includes numerical models, bench tests, full-scale room fires, and a small number of human trials. In fire-protective layers, PCM generally slowed heat transfer during exposure, yet part of the reported gain reflected added mass or thermal resistance rather than latent heat. Models of wetted fire-protective clothing from one research group predicted that heat released on re-solidification can cause burns that a PCM-free garment would not, particularly after brief, intense exposures or with melting points above 50 °C, and glove-sample tests showed prolonged post-exposure temperature rises. Removable PCM vests produced marked local cooling, but beneath heavy firefighting clothing did not lower core temperature, heart rate, or thermal sensation during exercise in the heat. Fiber-route evidence for occupational textiles stops at fabric characterization; laundering has not been linked to burn-protection or comfort outcomes, and no PCM-specific studies were found for arc flash, molten-metal, or welding clothing. Joint testing of exposure and cooling phases against thickness- and mass-matched controls should precede wider use.

Fiber-route evidence for occupational textiles stops at fabric characterization; laundering has not been linked to burn-protection or comfort outcomes, and no PCM-specific studies were found for arc flash, molten-metal, or welding clothing.

papers.title: Unveiling an antimicrobial nonionic surfactant with enhanced surface activity, emulsification, and physicochemical performance
papers.abstract: : A nonionic surfactant, tetraethylene glycol monopalmitate (PEG4-P), was produced with a 98% yield using a one-step imidazole-catalyzed esterification reaction. Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based fatty acid esters have been extensively studied, although low-molecular-weight tetraethylene glycol (PEG4) and palmitic acid (PA) derivatives are still relatively less explored. The synthesized surfactant was thoroughly studied using 1 H, 1 C, and 2D NMR spectroscopy, as well as FTIR analysis. PEG4-P has exhibited a lower critical micelle concentration (CMC = 0.0634 ± 0.004 mM). Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and dynamic light scattering (DLS) demonstrated spherical micellar structures with an average hydrodynamic diameter of 17.6 nm. Additionally, PEG4-P demonstrated better foaming performance, with foaming ability and foam stability of 84.38% and 60.38%, respectively. It has shown satisfactory emulsifying ability with coconut oil over time (1440 min) and created an oil-in-water emulsion. At the air–water interface, thermodynamic and interfacial parameters (Γ max , A min , ΔG mic , ΔG ads , ΔH, and ΔS) revealed effective adsorption and spontaneous micellization. Concentration-dependent MIC and MBC/MFC assays revealed measurable antimicrobial activity against Candida albicans, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus cereus, and Staphylococcus aureus , as well as Escherichia coli and Salmonella typhimurium . Thermal properties, cloud point, solidification temperature, and viscosity were also analyzed in this study. The study recommends PEG4-P as a viable option for detergent, cosmetic, and antibacterial formulations due to its superior emulsifying ability and advantageous physicochemical characteristics.

Concentration-dependent MIC and MBC/MFC assays revealed measurable antimicrobial activity against Candida albicans, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus cereus, and Staphylococcus aureus , as well as Escherichia coli and Salmonella typhimurium .

papers.title: A multiphysics computational framework for evaluating ATP response and thermal loading during skeletal muscle photobiomodulation
papers.abstract: Photobiomodulation outcomes depend on how light delivery, tissue heating, and cellular energy-related activity change together. This study develops a three-dimensional computational framework that combines light transport, heat transfer, and a phenomenological model of adenosine triphosphate-related activity in layered skin, fat, and skeletal muscle. The model compares wavelengths of 810, 850, and 900 nm and evaluates the effects of optical power, beam radius, and a 180 s exposure period. Under the common optical condition, 900 nm produces the highest average and maximum light levels in muscle, whereas 850 nm provides an intermediate response and is retained as a representative wavelength for the coupled analyses. Increasing the beam radius markedly reduces local light concentration near the tissue surface while producing little change in the average light level within muscle. At 850 nm with a Gaussian \(1/e^2\) beam radius of \(w=4\) mm, the modeled muscle-averaged ATP-related response increases at low optical power, reaches a near-flat maximum of approximately 14.73% between 0.50 and 0.75 W, and then gradually decreases to approximately 12.29% at 2.50 W. In contrast, maximum tissue temperature and cumulative thermal exposure increase continuously with optical power. At 0.75 W, the maximum temperature is 38.584 \(^\circ \textrm{C}\) , while at 2.50 W it rises to 45.857 \(^\circ \textrm{C}\) . A local sensitivity analysis further shows that the magnitude and location of the modeled response maximum depend on the selected inhibition threshold. The results show that greater light delivery does not necessarily produce a greater modeled cellular energy response and may instead increase thermal loading. The framework supports comparison of coupled optical, thermal, and biological trends, but its predictions remain conditional on the selected tissue properties, geometry, and phenomenological parameters. Experimental measurements and higher-fidelity light-transport models are required before quantitative physiological or clinical interpretation.
papers.summary: Photobiomodulation outcomes depend on how light delivery, tissue heating, and cellular energy-related activity change together. A local sensitivity analysis further shows that the magnitude and location of the modeled response maximum depend on the selected inhibition threshold. The results show that greater light delivery does not necessarily produce a greater modeled cellular energy response and may instead increase thermal loading.

papers.title: ANÁLISE ESPACIAL DOS ACIDENTES COM ANIMAIS PEÇONHENTOS NO MARANHÃO ENTRE OS ANOS DE 2007 E 2021
papers.abstract: Objetivo: Buscou-se identificar padrões espaciais de distribuição de acidentes por animais peçonhentos no Maranhão, Brasil, entre os anos de 2007 e 2021. Métodos: É um estudo ecológico, com análise de estatística espacial por acidentes com animais peçonhentos. Os índices de Moran global e local foram aplicados para estimar a correlação espacial e a autocorrelação local, ajudando a identificar sub-regiões de acoplamento espacial. Resultados: Ocorreram 44.403 acidentes com animais peçonhentos, durante o período de 15 anos, sendo 70% do sexo masculino (TMA 29,3); faixa etária entre 20 e 39 anos (36%; Taxa Média Anual - TMA 15,4), 1.649 casos graves (4,1%; TMA 1,6), 260 óbitos (0,6%; TMA 0,3), sendo 24.789 (61,9%; TMA 24,2) por serpentes, escorpiões 13.881 (26,9%; TMA 13,2) e aranha 1.841 (3,7%; TMA 1,8). Com tendência de aumento anual na maioria das variáveis estudadas (p<0,05). O município com maior taxa foi São Pedro dos Crentes com 222 casos (TMA 323,24). Os índices de Moran global mostraram distribuição de cluster espacial estatisticamente significativo em todos os triênios (p-0,01; p-0,02). Conclusões: Desta forma, foram identificadas áreas com maior necessidade de intervenção, tornando-se possível planejar políticas públicas sobre a temática.

papers.title: Bifunctional MXene-Pd multilayer electrodes enabling coupled electrochemical reforming and hydrogen evolution
papers.abstract: Abstract Conventional water splitting requires high overpotentials, whereas electrochemical reforming offers a sustainable route to produce hydrogen while oxidizing alcohols. In this work, we report the rational design of structurally ordered multilayer thin-film electrodes via electrostatic layer-by-layer (LbL) assembly, employing palladium nanoparticles (Pd NPs) as active electrocatalytic sites for both methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), and MXene as a multifunctional conductive support. The sequential assembly of negatively charged MXene nanosheets and positively charged Pd NPs produced well-defined (MXene/Pd) multilayers, which delivered a high MOR current density of 9.38 mA cm − 2 . This performance significantly surpasses that of other Pd-based multilayer electrodes, primarily due to the role of MXene in preventing NPs agglomeration, providing superior electrical conductivity, and, in the case of HER, contributing its own intrinsic hydrogen adsorption-desorption activity, which synergistically enhances the overall catalytic performance together with Pd. Furthermore, in two-electrode full-cell configurations, peak voltages of 0.9 V with a Pt cathode and 0.65 V with a (MXene/Pd) cathode were achieved, both below the theoretical water-splitting voltage of 1.23 V. The cooperative integration of Pd and MXene thus maximizes both methanol oxidation and hydrogen evolution, presenting a viable alternative to Pt-based catalysts. This study highlights the potential of LbL-engineered hybrid electrodes as a scalable and high-performance platform for electrochemical reforming and clean energy applications.

papers.title: Electrification pathways for passenger cars: A comparative analysis of China and Europe
papers.abstract: China and Europe have made significant progress in the electrification of mobility, but they differ substantially in their policy approaches and institutional frameworks. This paper presents a comparative analysis of their electrification pathways, focusing on the motivations, policy strategies, and challenges associated with scaling up electric-vehicle adoption. The study aims to: (i) examine the policy measures implemented in each region; (ii) assess outcomes in terms of market growth, infrastructure development, and industrial competitiveness; and (iii) identify key similarities and differences while deriving lessons to support transport-sector decarbonization. The comparison of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and comparable diesel vehicles shows substantial regional differences in economic competitiveness. Based on Total Cost of Ownership analysis, BEVs are approximately 17% cheaper than diesel vehicles in China, while diesel vehicles remain about 25% cheaper than BEVs in Europe, reflecting differences in policy, market, energy, and industrial conditions. China's state-led approach has supported rapid market expansion, cost reductions, and industrial competitiveness, with local governments implementing targeted measures to promote battery-electric-vehicle adoption. In contrast, Europe relies more heavily on cooperation between public and private stakeholders, emphasizing lifecycle sustainability and cross-border infrastructure development. However, Europe's dependence on imported battery materials creates vulnerabilities within its supply chain.

papers.title: Sleep disordered breathing and neurobehavioral sleep patterns in children with congenital heart disease in southeast Nigeria
papers.abstract: Background Sleep disorders are increasingly recognized as important but underdiagnosed comorbidities in children with congenital heart disease (CHD). These disorders may adversely affect cardiovascular health, neurobehavioural functioning, and quality of life. However, data on sleep disturbances among children with CHD in sub-Saharan Africa remain limited. Objective To compare the prevalence and patterns of sleep-disordered breathing and other neurobehavioural sleep disturbances between children with congenital heart disease and apparently healthy controls and to explore factors associated with sleep disorders among children with CHD. Methods This hospital-based cross-sectional comparative study was conducted at the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital, Enugu, Nigeria, between January 2022 and December 2024. Fifty children with echocardiographically confirmed congenital heart disease and 50 age- and sex-matched apparently healthy controls were enrolled consecutively. Sleep patterns were assessed using the Bergersen Sleep and Speech Questionnaire, a validated caregiver-administered instrument. Demographic and clinical characteristics were compared between groups using the chi-square test, Fisher’s exact test, and Student’s t-test, as appropriate. Multivariable logistic regression was used to explore factors associated with sleep disorders among children with CHD. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Children with congenital heart disease had a significantly higher prevalence of sleep disorders than controls (32.0% vs. 12.0%; p = 0.016). Symptoms suggestive of sleep-disordered breathing, including interrupted snoring with apnoeic episodes, witnessed cessation of breathing, and mouth breathing during sleep, were significantly more common among children with CHD. They also demonstrated higher frequencies of behavioural and neurocognitive sleep-related disturbances, including attention difficulties, poor concentration, nightmares, headaches, and poorer school performance. In multivariable logistic regression, low socioeconomic status was independently associated with sleep disorders (adjusted OR = 2.89; 95% CI: 1.01–8.27; p = 0.047). Given the small sample size and limited number of outcome events, these estimates should be interpreted cautiously. Conclusion Children with congenital heart disease demonstrated a substantially greater burden of sleep-disordered breathing and other neurobehavioural sleep disturbances than apparently healthy children. Routine screening for sleep disorders using validated assessment tools should be considered as part of comprehensive paediatric cardiology care to facilitate early recognition and appropriate intervention. Larger multicentre prospective studies incorporating objective sleep assessment methods are needed to confirm these findings.
papers.summary: Background Sleep disorders are increasingly recognized as important but underdiagnosed comorbidities in children with congenital heart disease (CHD). They also demonstrated higher frequencies of behavioural and neurocognitive sleep-related disturbances, including attention difficulties, poor concentration, nightmares, headaches, and poorer school performance. Larger multicentre prospective studies incorporating objective sleep assessment methods are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Mechanical and Sound Absorption Properties of EUG / CIIR Vulcanized With Phenol‐Formaldehyde Resin
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Eucommia ulmoides gum (EUG) was incorporated into chlorinated isobutylene isoprene rubber (CIIR) and vulcanized using phenol‐formaldehyde (PF) resin and/or sulfur to produce EUG/CIIR rubber blend with various EUG contents. The mechanical properties, damping behavior, and sound absorption performance of the blends were evaluated. The results showed that the blends vulcanized by a dual‐curing system composed of phenol formaldehyde resin (5% of CIIR weight) and sulfur exhibit superior mechanical and sound absorption performances. With increasing EUG content, the tensile strength, hardness, and rebound resilience increased. The blends consisting of CIIR/EUG (80/20 w/w) show a maximum elongation at break of 1137% and a sound absorption coefficient of 0.72. Dynamic mechanical analysis indicated that the damping peak decreased gradually with increasing EUG content, and sound absorption demonstrated a maximum at 20% EUG. SEM and DSC measurements revealed that a sea‐island morphology is present in blends at 10 ~ 20% EUG, in which EUG microcrystallites were dispersed uniformly in the CIIR phase; phase separation occurred while the EUG content is 50%, accompanied by a sharp decrease of sound absorption, suggesting that uniformly dispersed EUG microcrystallite domains can enhance sound absorption, probably as a result of multiple reflections of sound waves within crystalline regions and scattering between the EUG/CIIR interface.

papers.title: Fatigue crack growth in elastomers for leading-edge erosion protection of wind turbine blades
papers.abstract: Abstract. Fatigue crack growth has been observed as a prominent damage mode in rain erosion of wind-turbine blades, where it is driven by cyclic pulse loading from liquid-droplet impacts. This study investigates fatigue crack growth in a thermoplastic polyurethane elastomer used for leading-edge protection, linking repeated droplet impacts to controlled cyclic loading in a lab test. The plane-strain tensile double-slit test method is employed to determine the actual tearing energy during fatigue crack growth. A new analysis technique evaluates tearing energy throughout the test by tracking strain energy evolution with crack length. A novel test fixture with circular grip faces was developed to ensure efficient gripping of polymer sheets. It is examined how dwell time (the interval between sinusoidal load pulses) affects fatigue crack growth per cycle, denoted as da/dN. The material exhibits pronounced visco-elastic behavior, including cyclic stress softening. It may take several hundred cycles to stabilize with repeatable stress–strain loops, requiring a run-in period before crack growth assessment. Tests with shorter dwell times need more cycles to reach stabilization. Two dwell times are applied: 0.1 s and 1.0 s. Longer dwell times allow greater recovery between load pulses, reducing cyclic softening. When da/dN is plotted against peak strain, the cracks grow faster at longer dwell times. However, when plotted against tearing energy, the data collapses onto a single curve, indicating that tearing energy governs fatigue crack growth independently of dwell time. Measured crack growth rates span from 0.6 · 10−3 mm to 10 · 10−3 mm per cycle, while tearing energies below a threshold of approximately 2100 J/m2 result in significantly lower growth values of 3 · 10−6 mm to 6 · 10−6 mm per cycle. This testing approach is novel for leading-edge protection materials, and crack growth resistance could become a key parameter in standards, material development, and erosion-safe turbine operation.

Measured crack growth rates span from 0.6 · 10−3 mm to 10 · 10−3 mm per cycle, while tearing energies below a threshold of approximately 2100 J/m2 result in significantly lower growth values of 3 · 10−6 mm to 6 · 10−6 mm per cycle. This testing approach is novel for leading-edge protection materials, and crack growth resistance could become a key parameter in standards, material development, and erosion-safe turbine operation.

papers.title: Distilling First-Principles Accuracy into Compact Machine Learning Potentials for Condensed-Phase Chemistry
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have made first-principles-quality potential energy surfaces increasingly accessible for condensed-phase chemistry, but their inference cost can still limit the sampling needed to compute experimentally relevant observables. In this work, we use knowledge distillation to construct compact “student” models that retain the accuracy of much larger “teacher” models obtained through either finetuning of foundation models or Δ-learning. The resulting students reduce production simulation cost by approximately an order of magnitude, making high-accuracy sampling practical for challenging condensed-phase problems. We demonstrate this across three problems of increasing sampling complexity: finite-temperature NPT simulations of ice Ih, classical and path-integral simulations of liquid water over 240–370 K, and path-integral umbrella-sampling simulations of water dissociation at the anatase TiO2(101)/water interface. When compared, the distilled students reproduce the target observables of their teachers more reliably than equally compact models trained only on the available reference data. The liquid water student, distilled from a Δ-learned CCSD(T)-quality teacher, reproduces thermodynamic, structural, transport, and nuclear quantum effects over the full temperature range studied. At the TiO2/water interface, knowledge distillation makes PIMD umbrella sampling practical and shows that nuclear quantum effects lower the dissociation barrier by approximately 2 kcal/mol and shift the molecular–dissociated free energy difference into closer agreement with recent solid-state 17O NMR measurements. Our work demonstrates how knowledge distillation can make accurate MLIPs practical for the sampling methods needed to connect condensed-phase reaction thermodynamics with experiment, notably for interfacial chemistry and catalysis.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of pyrolysis oils derived from lignocellulosic biomass and municipal solid waste as potential bitumen modifiers
papers.abstract: The transition toward sustainable road construction has led to increased research on replacing conventional asphalt binders with bio-based and waste-derived alternatives. Bio-bitumen derived from lignocellulosic biomass and binders modified using domestic and industrial waste have shown significant potential in reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by up to 80%. Life cycle assessments have reported net-negative emissions for certain biomass-based binders. However, these alternative binders may alter the chemical and molecular compositions of the base bitumen, thereby affecting its physical characteristics and overall performance. Pyrolysis of biomass and non-recyclable waste is emerging as a promising alternative due to its chemical similarity to fossil fuel-based oils. Despite its potential, the performance of pyrolyzed oils is highly dependent on feedstock type and process parameters. This study investigates the chemical, thermal, and rheological properties of binders produced from lignocellulosic sources (pine needles, sawdust, and rice straw) and a waste source (municipal solid waste). Five percent pyrolyzed oil from each source was added to the base bitumen (VG 40 in this study) for laboratory investigation. Results show that pyrolysis oils are chemically compatible with bitumen, but the variations in molecular composition and their quantitative presence affect the binder characteristics. Among all the samples, pine needle (PN) feedstock and PN bio-oil exhibited a balanced chemical profile with lower polarity, contributing to improved compatibility with petroleum binders. PN bio-bitumen demonstrated the closest similarity to the base bitumen in terms of molecular structure, thermal stability, rheological and aging response. The study concludes that the performance of bio-bitumen is strongly influenced by the source of pyrolysis oil, with PN bio-bitumen showing comparatively promising results for further development.

papers.title: Thermophysical characterization, kinetic analysis, and multi-response optimization of paraffin wax/eicosane binary mixtures for lithium-ion battery thermal management system
papers.abstract: Efficient thermal management is essential for the safety, performance, and lifetime of lithium-ion batteries, especially in high-power applications such as electric vehicles, where elevated temperatures and thermal non-uniformity accelerate degradation. Passive cooling by phase change materials (PCMs) offers a compact, energy-efficient solution. In this study, eleven paraffin wax/eicosane (PW/E) binary composite PCMs were prepared across the full composition range (S1–S11; 100/0 to 0/100 wt%) for the Molicel INR 21700 P42A battery module. Simultaneous thermal analysis (STA) under argon (10 °C·min −1 ) provided combined DSC and TGA/DTG data. Increasing eicosane content shifted the melting peak from 55.00 °C (S1) to 40.26 °C (S11); total phase-change enthalpy ranged from 135.03 J·g −1 (S4) to 252.78 J·g −1 (S11), a net +35.3% from S1 to S11. A solid–solid rotator transition (24.98–31.50 °C) contributed 4.8–22.4% of the total latent heat and is critical for accurate BTMS simulations. TGA yielded onset decomposition temperatures of 170–222 °C, exceeding the 60 °C battery limit by more than 110 °C. Coats–Redfern model fitting identified D3–Jander as the best-fitting physically admissible rate function (kinetic compensation R 2 = 0.957); effective activation energies were 107.43–145.07 kJ/mol after excluding the S2 encapsulation anomaly. Filippov-based k(T) coupled with DSC-derived tanh β(T) functions captured up to a 66.6% conductivity drop across melting. Box–Cox RSM optimization (Stat-Ease 360) identified S6 (PW/E 50/50) as the global optimum (D = 0.861, β(40 °C) = 0.07). The resulting k(T), ρ(T), β(T), and Cp(T) correlations provide a self-consistent property set for passive and hybrid BTMS CFD, pending direct thermal-conductivity measurement on the composites.

papers.title: Ultrathin Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 -Based Flexible Solid Electrolyte for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract NASICON-type solid electrolytes are highly attractive for solid-state lithium batteries due to their superior ionic conductivity and low cost. However, practical implementation remains severely limited by their inherent brittleness, poor solid-solid contact, and severe side reactions with lithium metal. Herein, we report a flexible Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 (LATP)-based composite solid electrolyte film fabricated via an in-situ polymerization strategy. This film achieves an exceptionally high LATP loading of 90 wt% within a minimal thickness of 20 μm, ensuring outstanding thermal stability and safety. Crucially, the composite electrolyte delivers a competitive roomtemperature ionic conductivity of 1.5 × 10 -4 S cm -1 and an expansive electrochemical window exceeding 5.1 V. Consequently, symmetric Li||Li cells demonstrate excellent interfacial stability, sustaining over 600 hours of steady cycling at 60 °C and 0.1 mA cm -2 . Furthermore, full cells paired with LFP and NCM811 cathodes display superior long-term cyclability and rate performance.

papers.title: Meeting lifestyle recommendations among cancer survivors – a cross-sectional descriptive analysis from the Swedish CArdioPulmonary BioImage study (SCAPIS)
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to describe lifestyle patterns in relation to recommendations -including physical activity, diet, smoking, alcohol consumption, and sleep quality-among Swedish cancer survivors, stratified by sex and age. METHOD: A descriptive cross-sectional study was performed using data from the Swedish CArdioPulmonary BioImage study (SCAPIS). Questionnaires and accelerometers were used to collect data. SCAPIS data were linked to the Swedish in- and out-patient registry. Descriptive statistics were used to describe proportion meeting lifestyle recommendations in different cancer diagnoses. RESULTS: In total, 2576 individuals were identified as cancer survivors in the SCAPIS-cohort. The median age was 59 years, 57% were females, the median time since diagnosis was 13 years, and malignant melanoma was the most common cancer type (50%). Most cancer survivors in the sample met at least one lifestyle recommendation. Meeting multiple recommendations were significantly (p < 0.001) more common among breast cancer and malignant melanoma survivors than among other cancer types. Females were significantly (p < 0.001) more likely to meet multiple recommendations and were twice as likely (53%) to meet the dietary recommendation compared to men (26%). CONCLUSIONS: In this study of cancer survivors, differences across cancer types were observed in meeting multiple lifestyle recommendations. Most survivors met at least one recommendation, while the lowest proportion meeting the recommendations was observed for diet and alcohol consumption. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: These findings suggest that cancer survivors might benefit from secondary prevention strategies targeting lifestyle factors in general and diet and alcohol consumption in particular.

papers.title: Metabolic dysfunction in chronic critical illness: mechanisms, clinical consequences and therapeutic perspectives
papers.abstract: Advances in intensive care have improved survival from acute critical illness, leading to a growing population of patients with chronic critical illness (CCI), many of whom require prolonged organ support. This condition is associated with persistent catabolism, inflammation, and poor long-term outcomes. Understanding the metabolic alterations underlying this failure to recover may help identify targets for monitoring and intervention. This review synthesizes current clinical and translational evidence on metabolic dysregulation in CCI and discusses its implications for monitoring, nutritional strategies, and therapeutic interventions. We performed a narrative review informed by a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE followed by manual reference screening. Preclinical, translational and clinical studies addressing energy metabolism, mitochondrial function, autophagy, ketone metabolism, inflammation and recovery trajectories in critical illness were qualitatively synthesized. Available evidence suggests that patients with CCI exhibit persistent metabolic inflexibility, impaired transition from catabolism to anabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered autophagy, and disturbances in substrate utilization, including reduced ketogenesis. These alterations, together with epigenetic and immunometabolic reprogramming, may contribute to muscle wasting, immune dysfunction, and delayed functional recovery, features consistent with the persistent inflammation, immunosuppression and catabolism syndrome (PICS). Much of the mechanistic evidence, however, derives from preclinical or acute-phase studies, and validation of these findings in patients with CCI remains limited. CCI may represent a state of impaired metabolic and cellular adaptation associated with persistent inflammation, organ dysfunction, and failed recovery from acute critical illness. Improved understanding of these mechanisms may support more individualized metabolic monitoring, nutritional support, and therapeutic strategies. Further prospective and translational studies are required to determine clinical relevance and guide targeted interventions.

Further prospective and translational studies are required to determine clinical relevance and guide targeted interventions.

papers.title: Synthesis of MgO nanoparticles stabilized on coconut husk‐derived biochar via pyrolysis and their role in enhancing rice salt tolerance through seed treatment
papers.abstract: Abstract The pyrolysis of coconut husk (CH) impregnated with Mg(OH) 2 at 400 °C produced MgO nanoparticles/coconut husk biochar (MgO NPs/CHB) containing 1.29% MgO (w/w). The biochar yield from Mg(OH) 2 -treated biomass reached 51.47%, which was higher than that obtained from untreated CH (41.23%). The morphology and particle size of MgO NPs were characterized by scanning and transmission electron microscopy, with average sizes of about 24.4 nm and 28.4 nm, respectively. The structural and physicochemical properties of the material were analyzed using x-ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and N 2 adsorption-desorption analysis. Seed priming with MgO NPs/CHB at a concentration of 100 mg MgO/L improved the ability of rice seedlings to cope with salt-induced stress, as indicated by increased chlorophyll content, plant height, and root length after 7 days of salt treatment under 75 mM NaCl. In addition, MgO NPs/CHB priming alleviated salt-induced stress in rice seedlings, as evidenced by reduced activities of antioxidant enzymes compared to the salt-stressed control, such as superoxide dismutase and catalase, lower malondialdehyde content, and an increased K + /Na + ratio in leaves compared to the non-primed salt-stressed control.

papers.title: Candidate molecular endotypes and dynamic risk prediction in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease: a systematic scoping review
papers.abstract: Background Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-MDA5+ DM) spans pulmonary states from no detectable interstitial lung disease (ILD) to rapidly progressive ILD (RP-ILD). We mapped molecular programs and prediction evidence to determine how recurrent biological states may support dynamic stratification. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Ovid and Embase were searched from inception to 22 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR; evidence was synthesized across molecular and prediction domains. Results Of 4, 166 records, 2, 317 remained after deduplication, 349 underwent full-text assessment, and 95 sources (80 primary studies and 15 syntheses) were included. Type I/III interferon signaling was the most reproducible program. Myeloid inflammatory-remodeling, adaptive activation with lymphocyte or natural-killer-cell loss, vascular-coagulation injury, and immunometabolic disturbance formed additional overlapping axes aligned with pulmonary-state transitions. Clinical and radiomic models showed strong short-term discrimination; harmonized landmarks, calibration, geographic validation, and decision-timed molecular sampling would strengthen clinical use. Conclusion The evidence supports an integrated map linking recurrent molecular programs to dynamic pulmonary risk. A calibrated clinical–imaging backbone, augmented by parsimonious molecular modules with incremental value and updated at prespecified landmarks, offers a practical framework for prospective endotype validation and treatment-aware prediction in anti-MDA5+ DM-ILD. Systematic review registration https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2026.10.0018 , identifier INPLASY2026100018.
